column1: # Recorded deviations of the pinned decTest corpora: rows whose result token differs
# from the value this library returns. There are two kinds of row.
# The first kind (one row, `ln116`): both values are inside the tolerance of the
# specification (GDA 1.70 allows the mathematical functions a result up to one unit in
# the last place from the correctly rounded one). The corpus value is decNumber's and is
# not wrong; the held value is the correctly rounded one, which the library returns. The
# row is recorded only because the two texts differ. The stage judges such a row against
# the held value, reports it as the verdict kind `deviation`, and fails it if the result
# token of the row no longer is the corpus value recorded here. Nothing is reported
# The second kind (64 rows) is a subset row (official0, extended: 0) of `reduce`,
# `tointegral` or `squareroot` whose result keeps a positive exponent. GDA 1.70, page 55
# (Appendix A, The X3.274 subset), states for any operation that after the rounding of
# its result a positive exponent is reduced to 0 when the coefficient then has at most
# precision digits (rule P); on 2026-11-22 the maintainer decided that every operation of
# the library follows the text of that page. The corpus value is decNumber's (its
# reduce, tointegral and squareroot keep the exponent) and is not wrong; the held value
# is the same number with the exponent reduced to 0, with the same flags. A row is
# recorded only if it differs from the held value by rule P alone. Nothing is reported
# The third kind (3 rows, `res397` to `res399` of `rescale0.decTest`) is a subset row of
# `rescale` whose second operand is longer than the precision. GDA 1.70, page 56
# (Appendix A, The X3.274 subset), rounds such an operand to precision digits before use,
# and the exponent of the quantum is then the rounded integer (issue 764). decNumber 3.68
# refuses the unrounded operand 2.000000001 as not being an integer and raises
# Invalid_operation, which the corpus records without a value (`?`); the held value is the
# result for the rounded operand 2.00000000 (an integer), and the row carries the held
# flags in the eighth column, which the stage judges instead of the flags of the row. A row
# is recorded only if it differs from the held result by this cause alone. Nothing is
# Columns (tab-separated): corpus, file, row id, corpus value, held value,
# decNumber 3.68 value, what the held value rests on, and optionally the held flags
# (condition names separated by spaces; given for the third kind only).
# built with DECSUBSET=1 and run on the row; it is the source of the decNumber value.

column7: GDA 1.70 page 30 (ln): "rounded using the round-half-even algorithm" and "should be correctly rounded, but may be up to 1 ulp ... in error"; the exact value is -8.99999999999998784999918E-8 (CPython decimal, 50 digits), so the correctly rounded 17-digit result is ...878; the corpus value is decNumber's, one unit in the last place above and inside the tolerance (decNumber also returns it in the extended arithmetic, where the extended row lnx116 lists the correctly rounded value)
